text:
Jordyn: Quick heads-up — I'm splitting the routing module into `edge-routing` and `core-routing` to decouple provider usage. PR posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1234. Main risks: provider version skew, tfstate move, and k8s secretpath rename. Looking for quick :eyes: and any obvious gotchas.
Chris: Taking a look now. Is the state move happening in the same PR or separately?
Jordyn: Separately. First PR is refactor + provider blocks + pins, second PR will do the `terraform state mv` and import steps. Keeping the state move out reduces blast radius.
Lee: What exact provider pins are we adding?
Jordyn: Pinning `hashicorp/aws` -> 5.2.x (constraints: "~> 5.2"), `hashicorp/google` -> 4.9.x, and explicitly adding `required_providers` blocks so module consumers don't pick mismatched minors.
Sam: For the k8s secretpath rename — which service owns the mapping? Secrets-controller needs to update its mount mapping or the new path will break pods.
Maria: I can own updating secrets-controller and the chart. Need ~30m after merge to run a staging smoke deploy.
devops-bot: Deploy preview created for PR #1234 — preview URL: https://preview.redwood-inference/internal/1234 (status: pending)
Chris: When I run a plan locally I hit the intermittent plan flake: provider plugin disagreement between module roots. Repro command: `terraform plan -target=module.routing` — sometimes shows provider version conflict even though constraints look ok.
Jordyn: That plan flake is usually because of a stale `.terraform.lock.hcl`. Recommend regenerating the lockfile at repo root with `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=linux_arm64` so CI gets a stable set. Add the regenerated lockfile as a commit in the PR.
Lee: My local also failed installing providers until I ran `terraform init -upgrade` after adding required_providers. Might be helpful to add a note in the PR checklist about `init -upgrade` and lockfile regen.
Jordyn: Good call. I'll update the PR template section with exact commands and add the lockfile commit. Also adding an explicit `providers` alias mapping to avoid ambiguous provider sources across modules.
Sam: For the state move, can we have a dry-run plan in a temp workspace? I can run the import+state mv in staging and validate. Planning a canary deploy tomorrow 10:30 PT; will ping ops-oncall before.
Maria: After merge I'll bump the chart and run secrets-controller changes in staging, then coordinate the canary.
Chris: Quick nit — please include a short migration doc in the PR describing rollback steps if state mv goes wrong. E.g., how to restore previous state backup and undo resource addresses.
Jordyn: Will do. Draft migration steps will be in the PR description and a runbook gist: https://gist.github.com/jordyn/abcdef.
ops-oncall: Acknowledged — I'll be available during the 10:30 PT canary window. If you need emergency rollback I can assist with the state restore.
Lee: LGTM once the lockfile regen commit is in and the secrets-controller changes are wired.
Sam: I'll queue the canary and post status here when started.
Jordyn: Thanks all. Ping me if you find anything blocking — aiming to merge the refactor + lockfile commit today, state-move PR tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Chris: Thanks — leaving a small review now.
Maria: :thumbsup: sounds good to me.
Jordyn: tagging @ops-oncall in the PR for visibility.
ops-oncall: Added a short checklist comment on the PR about backups + notification channels.
